The *Kummaṅgapañha* ("The Tortoise", Mil 7.2.6) is an inquiry located within the seventh division of the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral connects the discourse thematic tradition with several canonical discourses featuring the tortoise simile, including the *Dukkarasutta* (SN 1.17), the *Kummopamasutta* (SN 35.240), and the verses of Upasena Vaṅgantaputta in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 10.6) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records three modern translations of the text in three languages [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates substantial internal reuse across the Pali corpus, identifying 417 matching segments across 52 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest matches are shared with other simile-based chapters of the *Milindapañha*, notably the *Meghaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.6), the *Kukkuṭaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.2.2), the *Sīhaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.6.1), the *Sakkaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.9), and the *Padumaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.3.2), reflecting the highly formulaic structure of the dialogues in this book [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora meeting its score threshold [DharmaNexus].
